proposal.title: Zimkalquel: a verifiable key directory
proposal.summary: Zimkalquel builds a verifiable key directory for users of encrypted messaging.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Users cannot see whether a server swapped the key of a contact. Users of encrypted messaging depend on key transparency every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a verifiable key directory called Zimkalquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Key transparency is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel, which 128 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on key transparency for 8 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/zimkalquel/zimkalquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.
